scenario.summary: SlippyNunchucks hijacks Sogou Input Method’s branded vocabulary promotion mechanism via DNS interception of insecure HTTP requests to deliver a malicious configuration. This configuration triggers the download of the DarkVigil implant, which is executed through DLL side-loading and maintains persistence by storing modular plugins within the Windows Registry. Command and control is handled via the custom Duplex Message Transport Protocol (DMTP) for tasking and data exfiltration.

hunt.name: SlippyNunchucks Sogou Update Hijack
hunt.description: This hunt targets a sophisticated campaign where the SlippyNunchucks threat actor exploits insecure HTTP communications in Sogou Input Method (CVE-2026-120422). By hijacking DNS requests for Sogou's configuration domains, the attacker serves a malicious configuration that instructs the legitimate application to download payloads into directories used for DLL side-loading. The hunt identifies Sogou installations, detects anomalous DNS resolutions to infrastructure outside of Sogou's typical network (specifically targeting Alibaba-hosted staging areas), and corroborates these with rare file writes by the Sogou component manager SGTool.exe. An agent weighs the timing and prevalence of these indicators to identify compromised endpoints.

nodes.label: Identify rare binaries written by SGTool.exe

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, LOWER(file_path) AS path, file_name, file_hash_sha256, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_file_activity WHERE LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%sgtool.exe' AND (LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.dll' OR LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.exe') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, file_path, file_name, file_hash_sha256 HAVING host_count <= 3 ORDER BY host_count ASC
config.description: Find rare DLL or EXE files written by the Sogou component manager to distinguish malware delivery from standard updates.
config.expected_signal: A file written by SGTool.exe that is present on very few hosts. Legitimate software updates should be prevalent across the estate.
